ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.29
ai.summary: Manicode package version incremented to 1.0.29. musings.knowledge.md updated with new prompt engineering notes regarding local edits and user confirmation. Scope limited to internal repo metadata and documentation.

eli5.text: The assistant's version number ticked up from 1.0.28 to 1.0.29, which for external users means nothing changes in day-to-day use, but it marks that the team shipped a small housekeeping release. Behind the scenes, developers added two rules to their internal guidance: don't rewrite an entire file when making a small edit, and ask for confirmation before making changes they aren't confident about, so future behavior nudges toward smaller, safer, reviewable edits.

ai.title: Replace readfiles tool with updatefilecontext
ai.summary: The `read_files` tool is replaced by `update_file_context`, which accepts a natural language prompt to select relevant files. This change moves file context management from explicit path listing to an AI-driven selection process using `requestRelevantFiles` with the new prompt. The system prompt now dynamically injects selected file contents via `getSystemPrompt`, removing the need for a separate `<relevant_files>` block in the user message. The `search_manifold_markets` tool is also removed from the available tools list.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant for help with your code, it used to need you to manually point it at specific files before it could read them. Now, you can just describe in plain language what you're looking for (like 'find the login page component'), and it will automatically find and bring in the right files. The assistant also no longer uses the old 'search_manifold_markets' tool, which was likely a specialized financial market search feature, and instead focuses on selecting files based on your natural-language request. This is live today - if you open the assistant and your file context is empty, it will automatically prompt you to describe what files you need, then pull them in for you.

ai.title: CLI output colorized with chalk
ai.summary: CLI status messages now use chalk for colorized output. File version navigation, response stopping, exit, and file change logs display in blue, yellow, magenta, gray, red, green, and cyan. Backend file reading prompt whitespace adjusted. Chalk dependency added to npm-app.

eli5.text: When you run the tool from the command line, its text messages now appear in different colors: blue for file version navigation, green for loaded files, yellow for stopped responses, magenta for the exit message, gray for file change logs, red for errors, and cyan for file lists. You would notice the status messages stand out more instead of all being plain text. This affects only people using the command-line version of the tool, and it is already live today.

eli5.text: The assistant's software version was quietly increased inside one of its internal packages, from one minor release number to the next. This affects nobody directly: the change is confined to an internal file and no features, capabilities, or behaviors were added or removed. If you looked at the project's version history, you'd simply see this small numeric bump recorded alongside a few other similar internal housekeeping updates.

ai.title: Refactor system prompt for updatefilecontext usage
ai.summary: System prompt in backend/src/system-prompt.ts replaces read_files instructions with update_file_context workflow. Relevant files now injected directly into prompt context, removing need for explicit read calls before edits. Debug logging in main-prompt.ts removed. Typos fixed in request-files-prompt.ts. Scope limited to backend prompt logic; no user-facing CLI/Web changes.

eli5.text: The assistant behind the tool no longer needs to manually ask to see a file before editing it; instead, the files it might need are placed directly in front of it as part of its instructions. This only affects the backend logic that drives the assistant's behavior, so you as a reader won't see the chatbot act differently or the command-line/web interface change. If you were watching the logs or prompt files, you'd notice that the step where it explicitly requested to read files is gone and a couple of spelling mistakes in the helper prompts were fixed.

ai.title: CLI loaded files color changed to green
ai.summary: Loaded files output in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` changes from `chalk.cyan` to `chalk.green`. Complete message drops `chalk.green` styling. Adjusts terminal color consistency.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes loading your files, the list of file names now appears in green text instead of the previous cyan, matching the green color used for the 'Loaded files:' label. The success message that says 'Complete!' no longer has green styling applied to it. These color adjustments only affect how the text looks in the terminal window; they do not change any functionality.

ai.title: Refactor expansion prompt for diffs
ai.summary: Restructured `expandNewContent` prompt in `backend/src/generate-diffs-via-expansion.ts` to enforce explicit section identification. Added `<sections-to-expand>` block and `[ALREADY_EXPANDED]` sentinel to handle no-op cases. Updated test fixtures in `backend/src/__tests__/expansion-diff-prompt.test.ts` and `backend/src/__tests__/__mock-data__/graph/expected.ts` to match new output format. This reduces hallucination by separating discussion, expansion planning, and code generation.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes instructions that tell an AI assistant how to write code changes were reorganized to be clearer and more step-by-step, making it less likely to guess incorrectly when filling in missing parts of a file. This affects the internal system that generates code edits, and if you looked at the instructions given to the AI, you would see separate sections for discussion, planning which parts need expansion, and then the actual code output, rather than mixing those steps together. No visible feature for end users changes; this is stability maintenance to improve the reliability of automated code generation.
